newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee off peaks on arbitrage selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee off peaks on arbitrage selling.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures pared some gains in late business on scale-up arbitrage selling against New York but prices still finished up.
"Many are buying in New York and selling in London," said one. "This prevented London from rising further."
The selling centred on March and May contracts. The March/March arbitrage widened to a high of 79 U.S. cents a lb before ending the day at 77 cents, still up from 74.50 on Monday.
Traders said some light fund outright buying on the May position helped earlier gains.
By the finish, March was $28 higher at $1,559 a tonne after a session high of $1,578.
Traders said London's movement continued to hinge on the bullish New York market which was dominated by persistent speculative interest.

"The question is how long this (rally) is going to go on. It seems the specs have got a new toy to play with and they are playing to the fullest extent and there's no reason not to push the market further," said one.
"Furthermore, all the infomation that are coming in are on the bullish side," the trader added.
Traders said E D & F Man's coffee report released late on Monday contained no surprises and as such had no impact on the market.
Without giving figures, Man saw the 1997/98 Brazilian output significantly below 1996/97's but it did not expect the crop to fall to below 20 million.
One trader said Man could peg the 1997/98 crop at between 22 and 25 million bags.
On the physical front, traders said differentials for spot coffee had narrowed slightly as roasters rushed to plug nearby supply shortfalls.
For instance, the March coffee from Vietnam is being offered at $220 FOB under London this week, down from $250 last week.
In other news, Indian coffee exports could be down by as much as 50,000 bags this season on adverse weather and firm domestic prices. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
